subject: REM Sleep Turns the Brain Inward: New EEG Evidence of Sensory Gating
script: From Agewell Brief: REM Sleep Turns the Brain Inward: New EEG Evidence of Sensory Gating. A Swiss EEG study reveals that during REM sleep, the brain dials down external signals while preserving internal bodily input—a shift that may underpin memory consolidation and emotional regulation. Sleep is not a shutdown. It is a reorientation. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
